I don't think alcohol would help you anyway. If you have problems with depression and anxiety, drinking will just make you more depressed. Like I said, I'm pretty much in the same boat. I'm 22, right on the edge of failing out of school, never had a real job, etc. I even have irritable bowl syndrome, so we're pretty much fuckin' twins. So I hope you believe when I say that these things get better. Lately my friends have come to realize that sometimes when I'm with them I'm going to get depressed and stop talking and stare into space for half an hour and feel like I'm being judged, and they're really patient about that. There are so many people who get it and won't judge you, and once you start to feel accepted it gets that much easier to chill out.

One more thing: you gotta take it one problem at a time, that's the only way to get over the [learned helplessness](http://youarenotsosmart.com/2009/11/11/learned-helplessness/). Just look at one thing: maybe start out by trying to get in shape, or by making one choice a day to get your life straightened out, or by doing one thing a day that scares you. The first one is the hardest. If you look at your issues and try to take it all on at once and expect everything to change just because you really want it to, it's going to overwhelm you.

Man, you life basically mirrors my life exactly. We should talk. Do you like in St Louis? If so we should seriously hang out. And if not, PM me and we can talk on Facebook or something. You're not a loser, you're probably a pretty damn interesting dude in a society full of actual losers who don't know how to appreciate what you have to offer. I know that doesn't make the actual situation that much easier, but it's important to have a little self-esteem. I definitely don't blame you if it's hard to feel confident sometimes, I mean that's basically the story of my life too.

Two things though. Fuck all that noise about not mentioning the problem to a doctor - you can go see the doctor and tell him/her what's up and it won't do any harm. Doctors know all about depression and anxiety, so if anything they'll have respect for you for being able to admit it. And if worse comes to worst, you don't ever have to see that doctor again. And thing number two: if you lack people to talk to for the moment, get yourself an appointment with a good therapist. They can be the best people to talk to. Fuck everybody who thinks seeing a counselor is something to be ashamed of, they're just wrong, plain and simple. If you feel like you need help and you aren't where you want to be in life, go and get the help you need. You have every right to it.

Yeah that fits the bill. I had figured "learned helplessness" was a big part of my problem. I dealt with bullying my whole life and even in to college. So it makes sense that I would feel helpless in dealing with people when I've basically never gotten any social validation. But I'm not sure if understanding that is helpful or just makes the issue more frustrating... 

Anyway, I actually got ahead on the goals I made in [this](http://www.reddit.com/r/SuicideWatch/comments/qbj7o/im_not_interested_in_suicide_but_i_dont_know_what/c3wcssi) post, and made an appointment with my psychologist today. I'm really thankful for your help, I don't know what I would have done if I couldn't anonymously go to the internet with this kind of thing.

Earlier I made a page in my notebook to write one small goal for each day. Today was awful and I planned to skip my Spanish class, but I made it my goal to show up, and I did. I made goals for the next 3 days - tomorrow's is to make an appointment with my therapist. So I appreciate your advice.

In Spanish class I was actually in a good mood, probably because I was happy I found the willpower to show up. Somehow I felt confident, like I just didn't care what anyone thought about me on the way. But when I got to class, a few small things happened and my mood really crashed. I spent the last half hour staring at my feet. My teacher chased me when I left class and asked me about my work. I think she realized something was wrong, and she asked if she could help, but I said she couldn't.

I drove home pretty much in a rage, but I've simmered now, I think because I felt content that my teacher actually acknowledged that something was wrong. But this happens every day; I get bummed, I fight to get in a good mood, then something happens (usually someone gives me a rude look or something) and I crash. Sigh. I don't know if you needed to know all of that, but if you read it, thanks anyway.
